textbookText: Place the given piece of metal in a beaker. Cover it with a short stem funnel. Add water so that the stem of the funnel completely dips under water. Now fill the eudiometer tube half with bench sulphuric acid and half with water. Close its mouth with thumb (there should not be any air bubbles inside the tube). Invert the eudiometer tube over the stem of the funnel. Clamp the tube with stand.

Reaction between the metal and the acid takes place and hydrogen gas starts to evolve. The bubbles are seen in the tube. The gas collects in the tube by displacing water downward. (At the end of the reaction, the small piece of metal may come up in the tube. If it happens, give a slight knock near the metal and make it combined with acid). When no more bubbles are seen, remove the eudiometer tube closing its mouth with thumb. Then invert the tube immediately into a tall jar containing water.

Wait for few minutes and make the level of water inside and outside the tube equal. At this stage, pressure exerted by the given volume of the moist gas inside the tube equals to the atmospheric pressure.
Note the volume of hydrogen gas inside the eudiometer tube. Note the atmospheric pressure. Note the room temperature and aqueous tension at this temperature. Precede the calculations as below.

PRECAUTIONS
1. All the glasswares should be handled carefully.
2. There should not be any leakage of hydrogen gas.
3. There should be complete reaction between the metal and the acid.
4. Dilute HN03 can not be applied instead of dil. HCl or dil. H2S04
since HN03 acts as an oxidising agent for many metals and other gases (e.g. NO) are also evolved.
142 Practical Chemistry
EXPERIMENT NO. 3
Object: TO DETERMINE THE EQUIVALENT WEIGHT OF COPPER
AND TO FIND OUT ITS ATOMIC WEIGHT
APPARATUS REQUIRED
2. Weighing balance
1. Porcelain crucible with lid
4. Tripod stand
3. Asbestos sheet
5. Glass tube
CHEMICALS REQUIRED
1. Pure copper wire
2. Conc. HN03
THEORY

Equivalent weight of an element is defined as number of parts by weight of which replaces or combines with 1.008 parts by weight of hydrogen or 8 parts by weight of oxygen or 35.5 parts by weight of chlorine. The equivalent weight of copper can be determined by oxide formation method. Copper can not replace H2 gas from dilute mineral acids and it can form oxide with air. Being very less active metal, it cannot be completely converted into its oxide easily by simple heating with oxygen.
Therefore, it is converted into its oxide by indirect method. For this purpose a known weight of copper is treated with conc. HN03 f01101ved by heating strongly.

Cu + 4HN03 Cu (N03)2 + 2H20 + 2N02 2Cu (N03)2 2CuO + 4N02 + 02 The weight of thus formed black oxide is found. The weight Of oxygen combined with given weight of copper to form the black oxide is calculated. Then equivalent weight of copper is given by, Weight of copper Equivalent weight = weight of oxygen Since valency of copper in Cuo is 2, atomic weight of copper is given by, Atomic weight = Equivalent weight x Valency Atomic weight = Equivalent weight x 2

PROCESS
Take a clean porcelain crucible with lid. Weigh out the crucible with lid.

Weigh out the clean copper wire (0.2—0.3 gm) in this crucible. Place the crucible on the table and add conc. HN03 carefully with the help of a glass tube. Brown fumes are evolved. The lid of the crucible can be kept upside down to prevent the loss of copper nitrate solution. While adding fresh conc. HN03, rise the lid a little above the crucible. When all the copper dissolves in HN03, wash the blue liquid adhering on the lid very carefully into the crucible with a little distilled water.
